text: So the Swallow flew over the great city, and saw the rich making merry in their beautiful houses, while the beggars were sitting at the gates. He flew into dark lanes, and saw the white faces of starving children looking out listlessly at the black streets. Under the archway of a bridge two little boys were lying in one another’s arms to try and keep themselves warm. “How hungry we are!” they said. “You must not lie here,” shouted the Watchman, and they wandered out into the rain.
title: The Swallow Sees the City's Misery
director_note: I staged the swallow as the only moving actor, carrying the viewer's eye from merry windows to beggars, starving children, and huddled boys so the scene reads as a performed journey rather than a panorama. Keeping the bird in flight and the suffering figures painted into the city makes the injustice feel witnessed and inescapable.
